sentences: SEBI's cyber framework tells a broker to close a high severity finding within one week.
It never says one week from when.
So there's no date you can actually work out. Being confident about it doesn't help.

beats.label: A blank start
sentences: Open RegOS Sentinel cold and there's nothing in it.
No findings, no deadlines, no score, until somebody actually adds a document.

beats.label: Your own document
sentences: So you point it at your own circular.
This one's a real SEBI circular on transmission of securities, from July.
Thirty eight pages, two hundred and seventeen passages, and a deadline score worked out from that file alone.

beats.label: The gap, in your own document
sentences: Then it goes looking for one specific thing: a deadline you can't actually work out.
Page three. Monthly reports for a period of six months, and it never says six months from when.
Same defect as the opening, in a circular published three weeks ago.

beats.label: Caught, fixed, cleared
sentences: Here's that paragraph on its own.
Six months of monthly reports. Six months from when? It doesn't say.
RegOS reads it, gets the same answer twice over, and stops there. Fifty percent, and a case for a person.
Now the same clause with the start date written in. That edit is ours, not SEBI's, and the page says so.
A hundred percent. Nothing to raise.
It isn't hunting for something to flag. It's looking for one thing, and that thing is gone.

beats.label: The same thing, on the live product
sentences: And that's the live product doing it, not a drawing of it.

beats.label: Dashboard
sentences: With a document in it, the desk opens on four numbers, and all four are counted from what's there.
Open decisions, deadlines worked out, evidence still current, checks run.
One decision is blocking, and the reason for it sits right next to it.

beats.label: The workspace
sentences: This is RegOS Sentinel.
The bell shows what's genuinely waiting on a person, and the profile names the firm it belongs to.

beats.label: How it works
sentences: Before it asks you to trust anything, it shows you what it does.
Fetch the SEBI source, read it, compare it to the firm's control, record a decision.
And then stop, wherever the source stops.

beats.label: The source
sentences: Everything starts at the source.
The exact passage, the page, the question number, and a fingerprint of the file it came from.
Nothing's summarised, and nothing's made up.

beats.label: Live source check
sentences: A saved copy is only good as of the day you saved it.
So you can check that fingerprint against the page SEBI is serving right now.
Either way, you get a receipt.

beats.label: The gap
sentences: Now it reads the passage against the firm's own control.
The period's there. The starting point isn't.
So it won't work out a due date. It leaves the clock blocked and puts the gap in front of a person.

beats.label: A named decision
sentences: The decision belongs to a named officer, and the order it happens in matters.
You can't record a reading until every section the answer leans on has been opened and fingerprinted.
Then your own reading gets time stamped, before the tool shows you what it thinks.
That's what keeps it a judgement instead of a rubber stamp.

beats.label: What changes
sentences: Once the clock start is on record, the date works out and the checks pass.
One broad three month control splits into the two rules the source actually described.
A week for missing patches, three months for the rest.

beats.label: The record
sentences: All of it downloads as one report.
The decision, who made it, what it rests on, and the check codes tying them together.
A regulator can redo every one of them.

beats.label: AI assistants
sentences: Four assistants read the same corpus, and each one has a single job.
They work through fixed steps, and every step is recorded as it runs.
Then a tamper check recalculates the lot, so an edited step can't slip through.

beats.label: What it will not do
sentences: Each check tells you what it can't do, right where it tells you what it does.
It searches a pinned set of excerpts. It doesn't browse the web.
If a pointer leads somewhere nobody has committed, it says so instead of guessing.

beats.label: Ask RegOS
sentences: You can ask it something in plain English.
The answer comes back quoted from SEBI, with the locator attached.
Word for word. And if the corpus doesn't have it, you get nothing rather than a guess.

beats.label: Full record
sentences: It all lands in one ledger.
Who decided what, when, on what evidence, under which fingerprint.
This is the thing an inspection actually asks you for.

beats.label: Worked cases
sentences: Four worked cases ship with it.
Each has a cited source and an expected outcome, written down before it runs.
One of them runs against a real SEBI advisory.
RegOS Sentinel.
It shows its work.
And it stops where the source stops.
